failure.description: Canonical acceptance exposed three sequential contract/validator alignment defects: incorrect compatibility-schema lookup, legacy proof-record shape, and stale CI assertions referencing fields removed from the canonical schema.
failure.root_cause: Validation logic and proof record had drifted from the canonical NAYA_ACTION_V1 schema model.
failure.repair: Corrected compatibility-schema inspection, rebuilt the proof record to the canonical field structure, and aligned CI assertions with canonical verification/provenance/next_action fields.
failure.safeguard: Keep the canonical schema as the sole machine contract and ensure CI reads fields only from paths defined by that schema.

lesson: A JSON Schema document describes instance properties; its declared fields belong under properties unless the schema intentionally defines a custom keyword.
Required-field presence is not equivalent to schema validity when nested objects use additionalProperties=false.
CI assertions must follow the canonical schema's actual field locations; legacy convenience fields must not silently become required again.
The canonical proof record must evolve with the canonical machine schema, and proof scope must remain HEAD^ of the record commit.
Failure is repair information; stop at the first evidenced defect and continue the complete acceptance chain after repair.
